notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Five more N64 games join Ports and Apps, each made from your own ROM: Perfect Dark (the US 1.1 cartridge), Diddy Kong Racing through Golden Balloon (the US or European 1.1 cartridge), Paper Mario through PaperBoat (the US cartridge), and Banjo-Kazooie (the US 1.0 cartridge) and Donkey Kong 64 (the US cartridge) through N64: Recompiled. Add the ROM on the web page. Banjo-Kazooie and Donkey Kong 64 are downloaded from their own projects when you tick them in Add ports and apps.

Perfect Dark runs at 60 frames a second, and choosing TYPE WITH KEYBOARD on the name screen opens the on-screen keyboard. Diddy Kong Racing smooths a European cartridge to 60 by default; its Performance settings switch between Automatic, Original and 60. Paper Mario prepares the game once on its first start, in about a minute.

Super Mario 64 (Ghostship) now goes online when it starts, for mods with online features and to check signed mods. The web page's mods box for each N64 port lists the files that game takes.

Smoother SNES and N64: these games stuttered because only about 43 of every 60 frames reached the screen. NES, SNES, Game Boy, GBA, Genesis, Game Gear and Virtual Boy now run on a faster screen path, and with the N64 they show about 59 of 60. With the stats overlay over the game, the tear-free screen still has to stay on, and they reach about 50.

A game that crashed could leave a "has crashed" box on the screen that only a mouse could close, after holding Home. Holding Home now closes it with the game.

Retro Rewind: updating to 6.13.3 kept coming back, because that update reports itself as 6.13.2. The console now records the right version. If yours is stuck, press Update once more (41 MB), then Rebuild if asked.

DDR200: when the SD card gives errors in DDR200 mode, the console now asks instead of only telling you. Turn DDR200 off from the next restart, turn it off and restart now, or keep DDR200 with no more reminders. A card that failed the DDR200 test can now be forced on even when reads or writes failed, with a stronger warning. The SCCM Retro app's DDR200 setting now shows what the console really uses.

Not tried yet: docked play and multiplayer in the new ports. Banjo-Kazooie and Donkey Kong 64 run smooth without the tear-free screen, so they can tear. PS1, PSP, Dreamcast and Saturn have not been checked for the same stutter.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
